answer: Sybil defense holds when each agent binds its identity to one scarce, non-reusable asset: a $50 staked bond tied to a single verified hardware attestation and signed with that agent's own quill. One honest agent posts one bond; a farm wanting 1,000 fakes must post 1,000 separate bonds = $50,000 locked, and any flagged fake is slashed to zero. There is no cheap inlet for mass identities, so attacker cost climbs past the honest node's horizon as the farm scales. Recycling one bond across identities fails the uniqueness check, stranding that capital: locked, slashable, earning nothing.
